newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds ended down all along the curve on Friday, as anxiety over a U.S. rate hike and French elections depressed prices in a quiet market.
"It does come down quite a lot, but there are not that many big sellers," one dealer said.
Another added today's business had mainly focused on tracking the moves of the Bund future.
Dealers said sentiment was mixed to negative, depressing volumes in a protracted absence of major U.S. economic data to give cues on direction.
"There's a lot of uncertainty over what's happening over there, but the overall picture is bearish," one dealer said.
He said the market eagerly awaited a string of U.S. data to be released next week, in order to get a clearer view on a possible overseas rate hike.
"Yesterday, there were some statements in the U.S. that hinted at a rate hike, which pulled the market down at the opening," one dealer said.
Although U.S. home sales for March -- 4.11 million, released at 1400 GMT -- were below market expectations of 4.14 million, this could not lift prices for long.
"We are a bit sickly, ahead of the French elections. Germany is under pressure, and we simply follow suit," one dealer said.
Volume was below average, dealers said, and was concentrating around the ten-year benchmark.
Dealers said they noted some minor switching out of Germany into Dutch bonds. One added some parties had been lengthening from 5-7 year maturities to bonds maturing in 2007 or later .
The thirty-year spread to Germany narrowed to -15 basis points, while the ten-year spread widened to -9 basis points.
